$comment: This repository's own values for the review-evidence check in
@clossys/inspector (issue #403). scripts/collect-review-evidence.mjs
reads these; the package holds the grammar and the decisions, this file
holds the choices this repository makes and can change without waiting
for a package release.
requiredChecks is deliberately empty for now, not the live ruleset's 14
sibling required contexts. verify-standards.yml runs in a separate
workflow from ci.yml, under no ordering guarantee relative to it, so a
sibling context that has not produced a run yet grades
'required-check-failed' (a VIOLATION), not 'indeterminate' -- an
unobserved name is 'missing-required-check', which is a violation-class
rule; see ReviewFindingRule's own 'required-check-indeterminate' doc
comment in packages/controller/src/review/types.ts for why only an
OBSERVED-but-unresolved name gets indeterminate instead. Wiring the full
set in today would make every fresh pull request's review-evidence row
read VIOLATED for as long as its slower siblings are still queued --
the same 'workflow waits for provider-specific review evidence' shape
AGENTS.md's constraint warns against, just produced by CI timing rather
than a model reviewer. scripts/collect-review-evidence.mjs's own
--required-checks-from-ruleset flag (and deriveRequiredChecksFromRuleset,
tested in scripts/collect-review-evidence.test.mjs and exercised for
real in scripts/collect-review-evidence.integration.test.mjs) is a real,
tested capability for turning this on later -- it derives the set from
gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/rules/branches/{branch} rather than a
hand-written literal (#907), the same function scripts/land-stack.mjs
already uses for the identical reason. Turning it on here is a separate
decision for whoever owns the ordering question above.
requireApproval, requireSecondaryReview: false. Neither is merge-
blocking clearance yet -- this issue is about making review evidence
collectible and checkable, not about making review itself mandatory
(see the collector's own requireReviewPresence, set false in
verify-standards.yml, for the same reason). The unconditional rules
(a live unresolved thread, or a changes-requested review, at the exact
head under test) still apply regardless -- validateReviewEvidence never
lets a policy opt out of those two.
decisionUse is 'advisory' because requireApproval is false: an
'authoritative' decisionUse only has teeth once requireApproval or
requireSecondaryReview is true, and setting it now would assert an
intent this repository has not actually adopted yet.
